note: ISO 11940:1998 Thai transliteration, all tables. Working source: the Wikipedia presentation "ISO 11940" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_11940), CC BY-SA 4.0, retrieved 2026-11-19; used as the interim source pending acquisition of the official ISO 11940:1998 document, which remains the purchase of record for provenance. Rows in document order: the 46-consonant presentation table (44 consonant letters plus the ฤ/ฦ rows), the vowel-sign table (repeated ฤ ฦ ย ว อ entries deduplicated; ฤๅ/ฦๅ encoded as the constituent pairs), the isolated-lakkhangyao provision (ɨ), the other-combining-marks table (phinthu as ring below per the ISO column; the ICU CLDR implementation's ˌ is a recorded divergence), and the punctuation-and-digits table (paiyannoi reading ǂ for U+0E2F; the standard's angkhandiao reading ǀ is unrepresentable because TIS 620/Unicode do not distinguish the two uses). Expected strings are the post-compose (NFC where a precomposed character exists) forms. Excludes U+0E3F baht, which the working source's tables do not cover.
